files.role: Public lance.encodings schema describing Arrow-to-Lance array/buffer encoding trees associated with the 2.0 format. The header says it is superseded for 2.1, but actual cross-version use of individual messages must be traced before treating this whole file as unused.
ranges: SPDX license, proto3 syntax, lance.encodings namespace, and protobuf Empty import establish the schema.

The specification maps Arrow arrays to array encodings (potentially multiple buffers) and single-buffer encodings. Encoding applies the root then feeds child encodings, decoding reverses that tree. Structs/lists may span multiple physical columns, although an encoding here describes a single column. The superseding filename in the comment is encodings21.proto, whereas the checked-in next schema is encodings_v2_1.proto; the comment is not an actual import (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:6-9).

Buffer is a reference by buffer_index uint32=1 and BufferType buffer_type=2, where page=0, column=1, file=2 choose the buffer collection. Writers may choose placement for sharing, e.g. a dictionary in column metadata; this schema does not impose a placement strategy. These indices are not raw file offsets.

Nullable wraps an ArrayEncoding. NoNull contains values=1; SomeNull contains validity=1 and values=2; AllNull is empty. nullability oneof selects no_nulls=1, some_nulls=2, all_nulls=3. The comments describe one versus two versus no buffers, but child array encodings can themselves expand to multiple buffers, so these are logical components rather than a proven universal physical-buffer count (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:16-19).

List.offsets encodes num_rows non-null end offsets with the leading Arrow zero omitted. For row i, base is zero for i=0, otherwise previous offset modulo null_offset_adjustment. Non-null offset is base+list length; null offset adds the adjustment. Example [[A,B],null,[],[C,D,E]] with adjustment 7 becomes [2,9,2,5]. A single-list lookup needs only current and previous offset, enabling random access without a separate validity read.

The text says an offset greater than the adjustment denotes null and otherwise length is offset minus base. There is a boundary ambiguity: the preceding null formula can produce exactly the adjustment for a first null/empty value, so the strict greater-than wording cannot be assumed correct without decoder evidence (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:99-104). The range examples recover item spans using previous/end offsets modulo adjustment, with zero start requiring only the end index. Their 0..3-style notation appears to include list index 3 and must not be copied as Rust half-open range semantics. Offset scalar type is flexible and can be delta-bitpacked independently of the destination Arrow offset width. offsets is ArrayEncoding tag 1.

null_offset_adjustment uint64=2 must exceed total item length so a null marker does not collide with a valid end offset; the proposed optimal choice is 1+number of items to minimize required bits. num_items uint64=3 counts items referenced by this offsets page, allowing it to map to child item pages. Integer overflow and malformed offsets require implementation validation; none occurs here.

FixedSizeList has dimension uint32=1, items ArrayEncoding=2, and has_validity bool=3. Compression specifies string scheme=1 and optional signed level=2; the schema does not enumerate supported scheme strings, levels, or defaults.

Flat encodes contiguous fixed-width items: positive bits_per_value uint64=1 may be non-byte-aligned, Buffer=2 locates values, and Compression=3 optionally describes decompression. Bit width refers to uncompressed data when compression is used. Constant stores bytes value=1 but a TODO leaves literal encoding undefined in this schema.

Bitpacked uses compressed_bits_per_value=1, uncompressed_bits_per_value=2, Buffer=3, and signed bool=4 indicating a sign bit. BitpackedForNonNeg uses the same first three fields without signed. These declarations carry widths and locations but not bit order, sign-extension algorithm, packing chunk shape, or valid width combinations.

InlineBitpacking stores uncompressed_bits_per_value at tag 2; compressed widths are inline in opaque chunks. OutOfLineBitpacking uses uncompressed_bits_per_value=2 and compressed_bits_per_value=3, fixed across the whole buffer and described as transparent. Their tags differ from the similarly named 2.1 package messages; names do not justify interchangeability.

SimpleStruct is an empty encoding for shredded non-null structs with no data in its own column; validity support is a TODO. Binary uses ArrayEncoding indices=1, bytes=2, null_adjustment uint64=3; exact adjustment interpretation is not documented locally. Variable holds bits_per_offset uint32=1 without further offset layout rules.

Fsst contains ArrayEncoding binary=1 plus symbol_table bytes=2. Dictionary contains indices ArrayEncoding=1, items ArrayEncoding=2, num_dictionary_items uint32=3. PackedStruct contains repeated inner ArrayEncoding=1 and Buffer=2. These state nesting/storage relationships but do not specify FSST symbol-table bytes, dictionary null conventions, or struct transposition.

PackedStructFixedWidthMiniBlock has unusually capitalized ArrayEncoding Flat=1 and repeated uint32 bits_per_values=2. FixedSizeBinary carries bytes ArrayEncoding=1 and byte_width uint32=2. Block contains scheme string=1. The exact spelling/case is retained; none supplies numeric bounds here.

Rle miniblock metadata stores bits_per_value uint64=1 with documented supported values 8,16,32,64,128. ByteStreamSplit stores bits_per_value=1, described as 32 for float or 64 for double. GeneralMiniBlock composes inner ArrayEncoding=1 with Compression=2 applying to miniblock buffers; it is distinct from the later General compression tree message.

ArrayEncoding.array_encoding is the union of 21 declared alternatives: flat=1, nullable=2, fixed_size_list=3, list=4, struct=5, binary=6, dictionary=7, fsst=8, packed_struct=9, bitpacked=10, fixed_size_binary=11, bitpacked_for_non_neg=12, constant=13, inline_bitpacking=14, out_of_line_bitpacking=15, variable=16, packed_struct_fixed_width_mini_block=17, block=18, rle=19, general_mini_block=20, byte_stream_split=21. Dispatch must use this namespace/tag contract, not assume similarity with CompressiveEncoding.

ZoneIndex wraps ColumnEncoding inner=3 with rows_per_zone uint32=1 and Buffer zone_map_buffer=2 for filter pushdown. Blob wraps ColumnEncoding inner=1 and marks a packed struct of u64 position and size. This Blob marker does not define the newer BlobLayout's null description rules.

ColumnEncoding.column_encoding selects protobuf Empty values=1 for plain column values, ZoneIndex zone_index=2, or Blob blob=3. Array and column unions operate at different layers; their tags are not interchangeable.
files.limits: No executable encoder/decoder, active-version dispatch, or bit layout is implemented by these message declarations. Legacy policy and current writer use require tracing each consumer. Explicit unresolved issues are List's strict null comparison and range notation (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:99-149), constant literal bytes (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:190-194), and the superseding filename (protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:10-12).

files.role: Public lance.encodings21 schema for structural page layouts and recursive compressive encodings. Despite its 2.1 name, it explicitly contains 2.2 and 2.3 extensions. The schema records contracts; actual runtime version checks, encoder selection, allocation limits, and byte serialization must be verified separately.
ranges: License, proto3 syntax, and lance.encodings21 package establish a separate namespace. Structural encodings describe Arrow list/struct structure; compressive encodings describe actual value compression. These layers replace the older array-versus-buffer framing for the described 2.1 format.

Counting terms are deliberately distinct. num_rows is top-level user rows; num_elements multiplies rows by fixed-size-list wrapper dimensions and is the flattened FSL input to structural encoding; num_items counts fully flattened repetition/definition events; num_visible_items removes events with no value. A FIXED_SIZE_LIST<LIST<INT32>> example shows why replacing one count with another breaks nested-array interpretation. Blank lines delimit the next section.

Structural encodings are called layouts. RepDefLayer records each peeled list/struct layer's interpretation: UNSPECIFIED=0 is invalid/debug; ALL_VALID_ITEM=1, ALL_VALID_LIST=2, NULLABLE_ITEM=3, NULLABLE_LIST=4 (null but no empty lists), EMPTYABLE_LIST=5 (empty but no null), NULL_AND_EMPTY_LIST=6. ITEM includes primitives or structs. Null and empty list layers are distinct even when neither emits a child value.

MiniBlockLayout targets small values where per-value transposition is expensive; comments describe sector-sized compressed chunks and bulk compression tradeoffs. Its prose also says an entire page must be read, which requires checking against the actual mini-block reader rather than treating it as established scheduling behavior. Optional-in-presence rep_compression=1 and def_compression=2 describe levels, value_compression=3 values, dictionary=4 optional dictionary encoding, num_dictionary_items uint64=5, and repeated RepDefLayer layers=6. Omitted rep/def/dictionary messages mean those components are absent.

MiniBlock num_buffers uint64=7 excludes repetition/definition buffers, whose existence follows their compression messages. repetition_index_depth uint32=8 must be at least one when repetition exists; greater depth enables nested random access (example depth at least three for rows[50][17][3] through five layers). Positive depth requires depth+1 u64 index values per mini-block, including leftover-item count so final-item validity can be known. num_items uint64=9 differs from page rows with lists. has_large_chunk bool=10 is documented as a 2.2 extension for chunk sizes at least 64 KB; this schema does not implement the gate.

FullZipLayout targets large values where transposition cost is relatively low, zipping buffers. bits_rep uint32=1 and bits_def=2 use zero for none. details oneof selects fixed bits_per_value=3 or variable bits_per_offset=4; prose favors byte multiples for large values but does not declare a validation rule. num_items uint32=5 and num_visible_items=6 are separately stored; value_compression=7 and layers=8 describe values/structure. These counts are uint32, unlike MiniBlock's uint64 num_items.

SparseLayout stores Arrow structure in layer-local slot domains, ordered outermost to innermost, with independently readable compressed value chunks. Fields: value_compression=1, num_buffers uint64=2 excluding structure, num_items uint64=3, num_visible_items uint64=4, has_large_chunk bool=5 choosing u32 versus u16 chunk-local value-buffer sizes, structural_layers repeated=6. num_items equals visible leaf slots plus one placeholder per list slot without children; null primitive slots remain visible slots. Thus a 100-slot primitive with 30 nulls has both counts 100. Structural layers can be empty for a flat non-null leaf when scheduling domain equals visible items.

Domains are [0,num_slots) coordinates. Outermost means page rows; each layer's child domain is the next layer's parent; the final domain has num_visible_items slots. SparseStructuralLayer.layer requires exactly one validity=1, list=2, or fixed_size_list=3 arm. SparseValidityLayer preserves num_slots uint64=1 across parent/child and records SparseValiditySet validity=2. The requirement for exactly one is a semantic constraint; oneof alone also admits unset.

SparseListLayer uses num_slots=1, num_child_slots=2, SparsePositionSet non_empty_positions=3, SparseCountSet counts=4, validity=5. Counts are positive and parallel non-empty positions; valid parents absent from that set are empty. SparseFixedSizeListLayer uses num_slots=1, dimension=2, validity=3, with child cardinality num_slots*dimension. Parent nullness and child coordinates are separate, and multiplication/consistency checks belong to implementation.

SparseValiditySet has Meaning meaning=1 and SparsePositionSet positions=2. Meaning UNSPECIFIED=0, NULL_POSITIONS=1 (stored positions null, all others valid), VALID_POSITIONS=2 (inverse). Empty and All position markers are separate empty messages. SparsePositionRange has uint64 start=1 and length=2; it is a start/count representation, not start/end.

SparsePositionSet.positions selects explicit CompressiveEncoding=1 for delta-compressed u64 positions, nonempty contiguous range=2, all=3, or empty=4. num_positions uint64=5 records semantic cardinality for every alternative. Explicit cardinality, range length, all-domain size, and empty-zero consistency are obligations implied by the contract, not validated by the schema.

SparseCountEmpty is empty. SparseCountConstant.value uint64=1 is the common positive child count. SparseCountSet.counts selects explicit compressed u64 counts=1 with cardinality inherited from the containing position set, constant=2, or empty=3 allowed only when no nonempty list slots exist. No separate count-list length is stored.

ConstantLayout generalizes prior all-null semantics at file_version >=2.2 to any page whose visible values are the same scalar. Repetition/definition buffers may still be required to explain visibility/null kinds. layers repeated=5; optional inline_value bytes=6 must be absent for all-null pages, at most 32 bytes when present, and only for a non-null scalar representable by one fixed-width Arrow value buffer without offsets or children. This is a structural page constant, distinct from the compressive Constant message.

ConstantLayout rep_compression=7 and def_compression=8 are optional message fields; absence means raw u16 levels, not no levels. num_rep_values uint64=9 and num_def_values=10 count decompressed entries. Presence semantics here differ from MiniBlockLayout's absent-level compression meanings (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:82-91).

BlobLayout externalizes large binary payloads and stores position/size descriptions. (position=0,size=0) means empty; (nonzero position,size=0) means null and position carries repdef. inner_layout PageLayout=1 encodes descriptions with exactly one all-valid-item repdef layer, while outer layers repeated=2 describe original structure. Conflating zero-length null and empty corrupts semantics.

PageLayout.layout selects MiniBlockLayout=1, ConstantLayout=2, FullZipLayout=3, BlobLayout=4, SparseLayout=5. The sparse arm explicitly requires file version 2.3 or later. Constant's non-null extension and MiniBlock large-chunk extension have their own 2.2 statements; the file's 2.1 name is not a universal gate (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290).

Compressive encodings form a recursive tree: an initial array becomes interpreted data blocks and finally fully compressed page buffers at leaves. Data-block kinds are fixed-width, variable-width, and packed struct; ordinary structs belong to structural encoding. A buffer has no further interpreted decomposition at this layer.

CompressionScheme enumerates UNSPECIFIED=0, LZ4=1, ZSTD=2. BufferCompression.scheme=1 and optional signed level=2 apply to a whole buffer. Absent level uses a scheme-specific default whose number is not stated. General buffer compression makes a parent opaque even if its ordinary encoding is transparent. Higher levels generally trade CPU for compression, but no measured complexity is given.

Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407).

Compressive Constant accepts any block, stores optional bytes value=1 in metadata, emits no output buffers, and leaves literal encoding as a TODO. OutOfLineBitpacking reduces fixed-width values by removing redundant upper bits; uncompressed_bits_per_value uint64=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3 describe the result. Prose says compressed width is fixed and stored in this message, but there is no direct compressed-width scalar here; it must be recovered through nested encoding/implementation. Do not copy the old package's compressed_bits_per_value tag into this schema.

InlineBitpacking stores original width uint64=1 and optional BufferCompression values=2. Compressed widths live inline per chunk, allowing variation to tolerate outliers; the encoding is opaque and turns a fixed-width data block into one buffer. Chunk header byte layout is not specified here.

Fsst uses one page-wide symbol table stored in bytes symbol_table=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=2 for the transformed variable-width block. The contract calls the transform transparent. It does not specify symbol-table serialization or the FSST algorithm itself.

Dictionary maps a data block of any kind to a same-kind dictionary and fixed-width indices, recursively compressed by indices=1 and items=2; num_dictionary_items uint32=3 stores dictionary size. It is opaque unless dictionary content is considered metadata. Index widths, null conventions, invalid-index errors, and metadata placement require implementation evidence.

Rle emits same-kind run values and fixed-width run lengths, represented by CompressiveEncoding values=1 and run_lengths=2. It is opaque unless lengths are metadata. Unlike the older Rle declaration, it does not directly carry bits_per_value; the value-width description lives in the nested encoding.

FixedSizeList is a transparent structural flattening transform within the compressive tree, converting wide/fewer fixed-width items to narrower/more items without itself compressing. items_per_value uint64=1 is this layer's dimension, values CompressiveEncoding=2 encodes flattened output, and has_validity bool=3 records validity buffer presence. This differs from SparseFixedSizeListLayer's parent/child-domain description.

PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675).

General wraps the output of its inner encoding, unlike other encodings' input-oriented composition. In mini-block layout it compresses the whole mini-block; in full-zip it compresses individual values. In the FSST/Variable/bitpacked-offset example, compression can apply to offsets alone, value bytes alone, or the combined mini-block, or combinations. General has BufferCompression compression=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3, preserving data-block kind. Choosing placement changes random-access granularity and what must be decompressed together, as an inference from the documented units.

ByteStreamSplit transposes fixed-width values into byte streams without reducing size by itself, then recursively encodes them using CompressiveEncoding values=1. It is opaque and keeps fixed-width block kind. The prose's attribution of upper bits to mantissa is not sufficient to define a numeric representation; this KB retains the text but requires implementation-level bit mapping before giving an exact algorithm.

CompressiveEncoding.compression selects flat=1, variable=2, constant=3, out_of_line_bitpacking=4, inline_bitpacking=5, fsst=6, dictionary=7, rle=8, byte_stream_split=9, general=10, fixed_size_list=11, packed_struct=12, variable_packed_struct=13. These tags and nested types are different from the older ArrayEncoding union. No unknown/unset variant handling is implemented here.
files.limits: Version markers are schema evidence only: 2.2 large mini-block chunks, generalized constants, variable packed structs; 2.3 sparse page layout (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:354-355; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:580-602). Runtime gating, structure buffer order/endianness, codec implementation, limits, and validation need further review. Multiple prose/declaration tensions are recorded above rather than silently resolved.
